title: aggrid returns cell type different from the input type for empty cells and int cells
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary aggrid returns float nan for empty cells instead of none cell type. the expected type is the same as input: str for str, nice to have even int for int ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python import os, glob, sys import streamlit as st import st_aggrid import pandas as pd st.header('st_aggrid.AgGrid') value_None = None data = [ {"text": "abc", "int": 0}, {"text": value_None, "int": value_None}, {"text": "def", "int": 35}, {"text": value_None, "int": value_None}, ] df = pd.DataFrame(data) gb = st_aggrid.GridOptionsBuilder.from_dataframe(pd.DataFrame(data)) grid_options = gb.build() grid_response = st_aggrid.AgGrid( df, height=160 ) st_aggrid_folder_path = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(st_aggrid.__file__)) for dir in glob.glob("streamlit_aggrid-*.dist-info", root_dir=st_aggrid_folder_path): streamlit_aggrid_version = aggrid_version = '' with open(os.path.join(st_aggrid_folder_path, dir, 'METADATA')) as file: for line in file: if line.startswith('Version: '): streamlit_aggrid_version = line.split()[1] if line.startswith('Current AgGrid version is ['): aggrid_version = line.split('[')[1].split(']')[0] break versions_df = pd.DataFrame({ 'package': ["Python", "Streamlit", "Streamlit aggrid", "AG Grid", "pandas" ], 'version': [f"{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}.{sys.version_info.micro}", st.version.STREAMLIT_VERSION_STRING, streamlit_aggrid_version, aggrid_version, pd.__version__ ] }) st.write(versions_df) with st.container(border=True): col1, col2, col3 = st.columns([1,2,2]) for index, row in df.iterrows(): with col1: st.write(f"index: {index}") with col2: st.write(f"text: {row["text"]} type: {type(row["text"])}") with col3: st.write(f"int: {row["int"]} type: {type(row["int"])}") ``` ### Steps To Reproduce Simply run the example trying different versions of the lib. I checked as regression for the str type, for the int type even 1.54.0 version returns the float type instead of int. ### Expected Behavior index: 0 text: abc type: int: 0 type: index: 1 text: None type: int: None type: index: 2 text: def type: int: 35 type: index: 3 text: None type: int: None type: ### Current Behavior ### Is this a regression? - [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: see the attached images - Python version: see the attached images - Operating System (server): Rocky Linux 10.1 (Red Quartz) - Operating System (client): Windows 11 - Browser: Firefox 151.0.3 ### Additional Information _No response_

A few notes that might help here, since I dug into this:

The `float`/`nan` you're seeing isn't actually coming from AG Grid. It comes from **pandas at DataFrame-construction time**, before the grid is involved. When a column holds integers *and* `None`, pandas has no integer-with-missing type by default, so it upcasts the whole column to `float64` and turns `None` into `NaN`:

```python
>>> pd.DataFrame([{"int": 0}, {"int": None}])["int"].dtype
dtype('float64')   # 0 -> 0.0, None -> NaN
```

On pandas 3.0 the new default `str` dtype does the same thing to the text column (missing becomes `NaN` too). Also worth noting: your repro iterates the original `df`, not `grid_response.data`, so what's printed is purely the input frame's dtypes.

To actually keep integers as integers and missing values as missing (not `NaN`), use pandas' **nullable dtypes**:

```python
df = pd.DataFrame(data).astype({"int": "Int64", "text": "string"})
```

Now `int` stays integer and blanks are `<NA>` instead of `NaN`.

If you're open to an alternative to the original `streamlit-aggrid`, I maintain [**streamlit-aggrid-v2**](https://github.com/lperezmo/streamlit-aggrid-v2) - a Custom Components v2 rewrite (no iframe), largely API-compatible. It restores the input dtypes on the data it returns, so with the nullable-dtype frame above a round-trip gives you back:

```
int:  0, <NA>, 35, <NA>     # integer-typed, <NA> for blanks (not float NaN)
text: 'abc', <NA>, 'def', <NA>
```

```bash
pip install streamlit-aggrid-v2
```
```python
from st_aggrid import AgGrid
```

I just released `0.2.1`, which also fixes a rendering bug where a DataFrame containing any missing value wouldn't render at all. Hope this helps.

You're right, the original dataframe is being examined, not the AG Grid response, so the difference is caused by new default str of pandas.
In the real application, the dataframe comes from st.connections.query, postgresql database. In some cases, I need to remove some rows and collapse the cell contents of some columns, then redraw the grid.
Finding a float NaN instead of str or None breaks the code.
As a workaround I had thought of considering the float type as None for the str column and perhaps that's the only solution, considering the new default.
Can I apply something like 'astype' on the existing dataframe?
I will try streamlit-aggrid-v2 anyway, possibly for new applications.

Hi [USER], thanks for the detailed report and thanks to [USER] for your response with excellent diagnosis!
After reviewing this, the behavior is caused by pandas' dtype coercion at DataFrame construction time not on the streamlit side so going to go ahead and close this issue as not a bug in streamlit.
